Factory Videos

How we make a video from an idea: the Scriptwriter turns your idea into a prompt, the Factory (Seedance) makes the video, the Editor adds captions and music. Watch the Loom first, then follow this step by step. Once you get it, you can make any video you can describe.

Version v0.2Updated 12 Nov 2026Owner KTool Factory · Scriptwriter · Seedance · Editor
Download PDF

01Watch first

Making a Factory video with the Scriptwriter (Loom by K, Kira). Watch all of it before you start. Come back to it any time.

Video not playing? Open it here: https://www.loom.com/share/254994aaec9f4164870fd5f9887987b7

The Loom doesn’t record the sound from K’s computer: you see the videos but don’t hear them. Most of the fixes in it were about her voice.

02What this is

Higgsfield copies a real video and puts her in it. The Factory makes the video from your idea, with Seedance. It looks a tiny bit less real, but you have far more freedom: any place, any outfit, anything she says or does.

2 levels of Factory videos1 · Factory only: Scriptwriter → Factory → Editor. This SOP.
2 · Factory + CapCut: more complex edits. Bottom of this SOP.

Videos made in the Factory (tap to play, ⤢ Bigger for full screen):

Factory + CapCut videos:

The tools, all in the Factory:

  • Scriptwriter: an AI that turns your idea into a video prompt. It asks you questions and remembers her past videos.
  • Factory: where the video is made, from the prompt and her reference pictures.
  • Prompt bank: videos that worked, saved to copy and build on.
  • Editor: captions, music, the text hook.
The one thing to understandAI is a very smart child. It does exactly what you say, nothing more. Every detail you leave out, it makes up. The more you tell it (what, where, how, and why), the fewer times you generate. Every generation costs money and time.

03Before you start

  • Logged in to the Factory (K sets this up).
  • You know her: her niche, her outfits, her friends and family in the Reference library, and what her fans love.
  • You have an idea: from your task, from the Prompt bank, or from your own head.

04Step by step: a video from scratch

1

Pick the idea

Three places to start:

  • Your task names a format (e.g. “Everybody stares at me”).
  • Prompt bank: videos that worked. Open one and see why it worked.
  • Your head: anything you can describe.

The Prompt bank has videos saved for every girl: pick hers at the top.

Before you write anything, say in one sentence why a fan would stop on it.

K’s example: “She’s a 10 but…” works because a Star Trek fan reads it as “she’s a 10, and she likes what I like”.

Why: a format that already worked will work again with her. You only change what makes it hers.

2

Scriptwriter → New chat → empty your brain

Open Scriptwriter → New chat. Start with “I want to make a video where @her name …” (the @ tags her, like in Higgsfield) and write everything in your head. Use the checklist in How to write a prompt, below.

Picked a video from the Prompt bank? Hover it and press the yellow Script button. The Scriptwriter opens with that video’s prompt already in it, so the AI reads the prompt and your changes together.

K’s first message (Kira):

I want to make a video where @Kira is explaining that she is a 10 but she loves Star Trek. She should first be in her room, then second scene she should be in a convention, something like Comic-Con. I also want her to have no shoes anywhere in the video. She should talk broadly about these nerdy things: she trains her aim with phasers, she always rewatches the episodes, she tries so hard to convince her friends to watch Star Trek with her. A nerdy older Star Trek fan watching this should feel seen and happy. She should wear the green Orion slave costume, her yellow costume and her custom black Star Trek costume. She must look exactly as she does in the reference images. She should be pretty shy throughout the whole video.

Why: every detail you write now is a mistake you don’t have to fix later. Long is fine. Your first ones will be longer than this.

3

New, or built on an old one?

Tell it straight: “This is a new video, everything fresh and original.” Or build on one: see Other ways to use it.

Why: the Scriptwriter remembers her past videos. If you don’t say it’s new, it may copy an old one.

4

Answer its questions, with the why

It asks questions before it writes the prompt. Answer every one, and always add why.

  • K: “The beginning is a voiceover, because it hooks attention and looks like a high-quality edit. The last scene is her talking, because it makes the viewer feel spoken to.”
  • K: “The green outfit first, because it stops the scroll, especially for fans who know the character.”

K’s full reply:

Firstly, yes that split works. Let’s add a 4th outfit. The fourth will be the custom blue Star Trek outfit. I want the beginning to be the voiceover of her (still shy), and I want the last scene to be her talking with the noise of the convention and the people and cosplayers around her. This is because the voiceover at the start will hook attention and let her act naturally, as if she really recorded it and took time to make a high-quality video, and the talking at the end makes the viewer feel spoken to. Barefoot the whole video. I want the green first, because it will hook people’s attention, especially if they recognise the character.

Its questions show you the gaps. 4 scenes but only 3 outfits? Decide: K added a 4th outfit. Someone else in the video? Say who, where and what they wear (K: her mom in normal clothes, in the back of the garage, doing mom things).

Why: with the why, the AI understands the feeling you want, and it gets everything else right too, not only the line you wrote.

5

Read the prompt, fix it before you generate

It writes the full prompt, scene by scene. Read it once, as a check:

  • Exact words she has to say: in “quotes”. K: she had to open with exactly “She’s a 10 but…”.
  • Every action in the right scene. K: she touches the phasers only in scene 1.
  • How she talks: “I” or “she”? K: “she” (an inside joke) in scenes 1–3, “I” in the last scene so the viewer feels spoken to.
  • Anything it made up that you didn’t ask for.

Then: “Make these changes only and write the prompt again.”

Why: a fix in text is free. A fix in video costs a whole render. But the real test is always the video.

6

Send to Factory

Under the finished prompt, press Send to Factory →. The prompt lands in the Factory with her model.

7

References: one per person or outfit

Add one picture for every person and every outfit in the video, in the order of the prompt: @image1 is the first. K: green, yellow, black, blue, then mom = 5.

  • Press + → Reference library → her name → pick. A real outfit and a custom one is a good mix.
  • Never zero. With no reference it invents the outfits.

Why: the pictures are the truth: the prompt writes the action and the camera, the pictures decide how she and her outfits look.

8

Duration: 15s, then Generate

Drag the duration to 15s for any video where she talks (it opens on 8s). 9:16. Press Generate. It takes 2–5 minutes.

Why: Seedance fills the time you give it. At 8 seconds she says the same words twice as fast, and it stops sounding real.

9

Watch it like a fan

Watch it all the way through, with sound. Then once for the picture, once for the voice. Write down every problem: too fast, words overlapping, wrong outfit, wrong place, anything a real girl wouldn’t do.

K’s first render: the look was great, the outfits right, mom in the back. The speech was far too fast.

10

Fix it in the Scriptwriter, again and again

On the render, press the small yellow arrow ↳ (back to the Scriptwriter). The same chat opens with Script from this render. Write:

  1. What was good (so it keeps it).
  2. Every change, with why, as detailed as your first message.
Video was good, I like the realistic feel, the order of the outfits was perfect, but let’s change these: the speech is way too quick. She should speak in grade 5 level English, cut 30% of the words out, keep it natural, slow and shy. For the third and fourth scene it should look like two different conventions on two different days. A real girl wouldn’t wear two outfits in the same place.

Send to Factory again: check the references are still there, 15s again, Generate. Repeat until it’s the video in your head. Some videos take 1 go, some 5, some 50. New ideas take more.

Why: the same prompt makes the same mistake. Once one is perfect, you never have to make it again: you and everyone else can build on it.

11

Ready to edit

Right? Press Ready to edit. It moves to the Editor. (Need CapCut for it? That’s level 2: download it instead.)

12

Editor: captions

Editor → All creators → her → the clip → Auto-edit this clip. It writes what she says as captions. Read every caption; fix or delete the wrong ones.

Why: captions are a must on every video where she talks. Many watch with the sound off, and reading and hearing at once holds them. Every millisecond counts.

13

Editor: music

Song library → a song from her niche, or a trending one she would listen to. Remaking a video? Use the exact same song. Turn the music under her voice: she must be heard.

14

Text hook (if it needs one)

A text hook stays on screen the whole video. Not every Factory video needs one: if she says the hook herself, the captions do the job. How to pick one: SOP: Higgsfield Videos.

15

Download, save

Download and save it in her Drive folder → Reels (SOP: Google Drive). Send for review / Save to bank: when to use which

05Other ways to use it

This SOP made a video from scratch. The same tools do much more. Every one starts in the Scriptwriter, with the same rules: say exactly what to keep, what to change, and why.

  • Remake a Prompt bank video with a change: same video, a different outfit, place or girl. “Make the [name] video again, exactly the same, but she wears her yellow costume.”
  • Take one part: only the beginning, one scene or one line of a video, and build a new video around it.
  • Build on her own past videos: the Scriptwriter remembers them. “Take the She’s a 10 video and give it a different beginning.”
  • For another girl: a video that works for one girl can work for another in her niche. Change the outfits and the niche words.
  • One simple action: one line is enough when the video is simple (K: “Kira does a backflip in the garden in her red uniform”).
  • A video from somewhere else: describe it to the Scriptwriter, or attach it (From a video). how From a video works

Made one that works? Save it to the bank: you and everyone else can use it. Tell your colleagues.

06How to write a prompt

This works for any video, any girl. Go down the list; anything you skip, the AI decides for you.

  • Who: @her, and anyone else (friends, family). What each one wears.
  • Scenes, in order: “first…, then second scene…”. Where each one is, day or night.
  • Outfits per scene, named like her references. Add: “must look exactly as in the reference images”.
  • What she says: the topics, or the exact words in “quotes”. “I” or “she”.
  • Voiceover or talking to camera, and where it changes.
  • How she acts: shy, confident, playful.
  • Rules for the whole video: e.g. barefoot the whole time.
  • The viewer: who he is and how he should feel (“a nerdy older Star Trek fan should feel seen and happy”).
  • Why, for every choice.

Fixing her voice (most fixes are here):

  • Too fast: “grade 5 level English, cut 30% of the words, natural, slow”.
  • Words overlapping: say so, in those words.
  • Too perfect: “she should stutter once, about 6 seconds in”. A stutter makes her human.
  • Not real: “a real girl wouldn’t…”. She’s a real girl; that’s what the viewer has to believe.

Who she is to the viewer: every girl has her own personality and her own things that work. Write her the way her fans know her, and build on what already works for her. each girl’s personality and deck (not made yet)

07Formats that work

  • Everybody stares at me: she films herself in a busy public place in an outfit from her niche, and talks shyly about everyone staring at her. Watch it in What this is. what makes it work, from K
  • POV: a text hook that puts the viewer in the scene (her boyfriend, her friend).
  • Talking to camera: she talks to the viewer about her niche; captions carry it.
  • She’s a 10 but…: she describes herself in the third person; the “but” is her niche. Each scene a new outfit and place.
  • One action: e.g. Kira does a backflip in the garden in her red uniform.

08Rules and nuances

  • Keep it simple, be detailed. One clear idea, every detail written down.
  • Talking video: 15 seconds, always.
  • Every person and outfit has a reference picture. Never zero.
  • Captions on every video where she talks.
  • Mistakes are normal. Fix them in the Scriptwriter; never generate again unchanged.
  • Everything right? Save it to the Prompt bank, so you and everyone else can use it.

quality setting in the Factory, and anything else

09Done means

  • The number of finished Factory videos your task asks for.
  • Each one: her, her outfits exactly as the references, a voice that sounds real and slow enough to follow.
  • Captions checked word by word, music under her voice.
  • Saved in her Reels folder in Drive. Reviewed with K.

10Common mistakes

  • A one-line prompt for a complex video. The AI fills every gap with its own ideas.
  • Leaving it on 8 seconds for a talking video.
  • No reference pictures, or in the wrong order.
  • Generating again without changing the prompt.
  • Not checking the captions.
  • Two outfits in the same place, or anything a real girl wouldn’t do.

Added after every review with K
